text: Which planet in the solar system has the strongest magnetic field, and roughly how many times stronger is it than Earth's field at the cloud tops?
What are the three domains of life in modern biological taxonomy, and which of them contains organisms with membrane-bound nuclei?
In what decade was the double-helix structure of DNA published, who were the two authors of the famous one-page paper, and in which journal did it appear?
Name the four fundamental forces of physics and state which of them is the weakest when comparing two protons inside a nucleus.
What is the difference between weather and climate, and what time span do climatologists conventionally use to define a climate normal?
Which country has the longest total coastline in the world, and name the three oceans that touch its shores.
What does the acronym LASER stand for, and what physical process inside the gain medium makes the emitted light coherent?
Who composed the Brandenburg Concertos, roughly when were they assembled as a set, and to whom were they dedicated?
What is the tallest mountain on Earth when measured from its base to its peak rather than from sea level, and where is it located?
Which metallic element has the highest melting point, and name one industrial application that depends directly on that property.
What are the primary colors of light in the additive color model, and what color results when all three are combined at full intensity?
In which city and year was the United Nations Charter signed, and roughly how many countries were original signatories?
What is the largest internal organ of the human body, and list two of its major metabolic functions.
Which ancient wonder of the world stood at Alexandria, what practical purpose did it serve, and roughly when was it destroyed?
What is the chemical formula of common table salt, and what type of chemical bond holds its crystal lattice together?
Name the longest river in South America, the ocean it empties into, and one country other than Brazil that its drainage basin covers.
What particle was discovered at CERN in 2012, which theoretical mechanism does its existence confirm, and which two experiments announced the discovery?
Explain the difference between a meteoroid, a meteor, and a meteorite, in one or two sentences for each term.
Which treaty formally ended the First World War between the Allies and Germany, in what year was it signed, and in which French palace?
What are the two official languages of Canada at the federal level, and which province has French as its sole official language?
Write a Python function that takes a list of integers and returns a new list containing only the values that appear exactly once, preserving their original order.
Write a JavaScript function that debounces another function, waiting a given number of milliseconds after the last call before invoking it.
Write a SQL query that returns the three highest-paid employees per department, given tables employees(id, name, salary, dept_id) and departments(id, name).
Write a Python generator function that yields the Fibonacci sequence indefinitely, then show how to take the first ten values from it.
Write a bash one-liner that finds all files larger than 100 megabytes under the current directory and prints their sizes in human-readable form.
Write a regular expression that matches ISO 8601 dates in the form YYYY-MM-DD, rejecting month 00 and months above 12, and briefly explain each part.
Write a Rust function that reverses the order of the words in a string slice while preserving single spaces between them, returning a new String.
Write a Go function that merges two sorted slices of integers into one sorted slice without using the standard library's sort package.
Write a Python class implementing a fixed-capacity LRU cache with get and put methods, each running in constant average time.
Write a C function that counts the number of set bits in an unsigned 32-bit integer without using compiler intrinsics.
Write a JavaScript function that deep-clones a plain object containing nested objects, arrays, strings, and numbers, without using structuredClone or JSON round-trips.
Write a SQL statement that creates a table for blog posts with an auto-incrementing primary key, a title, a body, and a creation timestamp that defaults to the current time.
Write a Python function that checks whether a string of brackets containing (), [], and {} is balanced, using an explicit stack.
Write a recursive Python function that computes the power set of a list, and state its time complexity in a one-line comment.
Write a TypeScript interface for a paginated API response holding items of a generic type, a total count, a page number, and a page size, then write the signature of a function that fetches one page.
Write a Python function that parses a single CSV line by hand, honoring quoted fields and escaped double quotes, without importing the csv module.
Write a Java method that returns the first non-repeating character in a string, or an empty Optional if every character repeats.
Write a Python decorator that retries the wrapped function up to three times with exponential backoff whenever it raises an exception.
Write an HTML fragment with inline CSS in a style tag that centers a card both horizontally and vertically in the viewport using flexbox.
Write a Ruby method that converts a snake_case string to CamelCase without using external gems, then show two example calls with their outputs.
A train departs at 9:40 and arrives at 13:05, having made four intermediate stops of six minutes each. For how long was it actually moving? Show your steps.
Today Maria is three times as old as her son. In twelve years she will be twice as old as he will be then. How old is each of them today? Show the equations you use.
A store discounts a jacket by 20 percent, then applies a further 15 percent off the reduced price. What single percentage discount is equivalent to the two combined? Show the calculation.
You have a 3-liter jug, a 5-liter jug, and unlimited water. Describe a sequence of fills, pours, and empties that leaves exactly 4 liters in the larger jug.
If five machines take five minutes to make five widgets, how long do one hundred machines take to make one hundred widgets? Explain why the intuitive answer is wrong.
A password consists of two distinct uppercase letters followed by three digits, where digits may repeat. How many such passwords exist? Walk through the counting.
A farmer keeps chickens and rabbits, counting 35 heads and 94 legs in total. How many of each animal are there? Set up and solve the system.
Starting from 1000, alternately subtract 7 and then add 3, one operation at a time. After how many operations does the running value first drop below 900? Show the pattern you use.
Three friends split a restaurant bill of 87 dollars. One pays 10 dollars more than each of the other two, who pay equal amounts. How much does each person pay? Verify the total.
A cyclist rides uphill at 12 kilometers per hour and returns downhill along the same road at 36 kilometers per hour. What is the average speed for the round trip? Explain why it is not 24.
In a class of 40 students, 22 study French, 18 study German, and 7 study both. How many study neither language? Use inclusion-exclusion and show each term.
A clock shows exactly 3:15. What is the angle in degrees between the hour and minute hands? Work through the position of each hand.
You flip a fair coin four times. What is the probability of getting at least three heads? List the favorable outcomes or compute with binomial coefficients.
A rectangle's length is 4 units more than twice its width, and its perimeter is 56 units. Find its area, writing the perimeter equation first.
Convert 72 kilometers per hour into meters per second, then determine how many seconds a vehicle at that speed needs to cover 450 meters.
Three runners finished a race. Ben was not last, Anna finished ahead of Ben, and Carl did not finish ahead of Anna. Determine the finishing order and explain each deduction.
A tank fills through one pipe in 6 hours and drains through another in 9 hours. With both pipes open, how long does an empty tank take to fill? Show the rates.
What is the sum of all integers from 1 to 200 that are divisible by 3 but not by 5? Describe the sets you count and the arithmetic series involved.
A book's pages are numbered starting at 1, and printing all the page numbers used exactly 552 digits. How many pages does the book have? Break the count into digit lengths.

Two candles of equal height are lit at the same moment. One burns down completely in 4 hours, the other in 3 hours. After how much time is one candle exactly twice the height of the other? Set up the equation.

Summarize the following passage in exactly one sentence. Passage: The lighthouse keeper recorded wind speeds every morning for thirty years. When automation arrived in 1994, his handwritten logs were donated to the maritime museum, where researchers later used them to reconstruct storm patterns that predated satellite observation.

List every person's name mentioned in the passage below, one per line, in order of first appearance. Passage: When Priya arrived at the workshop, Daniel was already calibrating the telescope. They waited an hour for Chen, who had promised to bring the replacement mirror, but only his assistant Rosa appeared, carrying a note of apology.

Rewrite the following passage in the past tense, changing nothing else. Passage: The ferry leaves the harbor at dawn and crosses the strait in forty minutes. Most passengers stay on the upper deck, where gulls follow the wake and the mainland slowly resolves into rooftops and cranes.

Extract all dates and years from this passage and present them as a comma-separated list. Passage: Construction began on 12 March 1931 and halted during 1933 for lack of funds. Work resumed in April 1935, and the bridge finally opened to traffic on 19 May 1937, eleven days ahead of the revised schedule.

Count how many distinct cities are named in the passage below and list them alphabetically. Passage: The orchestra's tour opened in Lisbon before moving to Madrid and Barcelona. After a week's rest they performed twice in Lyon, skipped the planned Milan date, and closed the season with three sold-out nights in Vienna.

Identify the main claim of the following passage and state it in your own words in no more than fifteen words. Passage: Although tidal energy remains more expensive than wind per installed megawatt, its output is predictable years in advance, which spares grid operators the reserve costs that intermittent sources impose. Predictability, not raw price, is the figure that should anchor comparisons.

Convert the following passage into a bulleted list of the steps it describes, keeping the original order. Passage: To graft the apple cutting, first slice the rootstock diagonally, then cut a matching angle on the scion. Bind the two surfaces with grafting tape, seal the joint with wax, and label the branch with the variety and the date.

Answer the question using only information from the passage. Question: why did the expedition turn back? Passage: At 7,600 meters the weather held, but two of the four oxygen regulators had frozen overnight. The team calculated that summiting with shared regulators would leave no margin for a slow descent, and turned back at noon.

Rewrite the passage below so that it addresses the reader directly as 'you' instead of describing 'a visitor'. Passage: A visitor entering the archive must first register at the desk and store any bags in the lockers. A visitor may request up to five boxes per day, and a visitor who needs photographs must sign the reproduction form.

Find the one internal inconsistency in the passage and explain it in one sentence. Passage: The museum's oldest clock was built in 1712 by a Dutch craftsman and has run continuously for over four centuries. It stands in the east gallery, where its original pendulum still swings behind the original glass.

Rewrite this passage in a casual, friendly tone while keeping every fact intact. Passage: Attendees are advised that the seminar will commence promptly at nine o'clock. Refreshments will be provided during the interval, and participants are requested to submit any questions in writing prior to the closing session.

Extract every number from the passage and output them as a JSON array of integers in order of appearance. Passage: The cooperative began with 14 members in 1987, grew to 210 within a decade, and today manages 3 processing plants, 46 trucks, and roughly 12000 hectares of farmland.

State whether the passage below supports, contradicts, or does not address this claim: 'The reservoir's water level rose in spring.' Answer with one of those three options, then give one sentence of justification. Passage: Snowmelt in April pushed inflows to their highest levels in six years, and by late May the reservoir stood two meters above its winter mark despite steady releases downstream.

Shorten the following passage to at most twenty-five words without losing its warning. Passage: Never mix chlorine-based cleaning products with those containing ammonia, because the combination releases chloramine gas, which can cause severe respiratory damage even in small, poorly ventilated spaces such as bathrooms.

Reorder the sentences below into chronological order and output only the reordered passage. Passage: The verdict was announced on Friday. Jury selection had taken most of March. The appeal was filed within a week. Opening arguments began in early April.

Identify the antecedent of each pronoun in the final sentence of the passage. Passage: The curator unpacked the crate while the restorer prepared the workbench. When she lifted the painting onto it, he photographed its frame.

Write a one-sentence headline of fewer than twelve words for the following passage. Passage: After nine seasons of decline, the harbor's herring catch doubled this year. Biologists credit cooler currents and the closure of two spawning grounds, though they caution that a single strong year does not yet make a recovery.

Classify the passage below as primarily narrative, descriptive, expository, or persuasive, and defend your choice in two sentences. Passage: The market opens before sunrise. Stalls of citrus glow under strings of bulbs, fishmongers stack ice into silver hills, and the smell of diesel and coffee mixes in the cold air.

Replace every passive construction in the passage with an active one, inventing plausible agents where needed. Passage: The samples were collected at dawn and were labeled before noon. Errors in the first batch were discovered during review, and a corrected protocol was issued the following week.

Produce a two-column table listing the animals named in the passage and their habitats as stated. Passage: The survey recorded otters along the riverbanks, kestrels nesting in the quarry face, and a small colony of natterjack toads in the dune slacks behind the beach.
Write a short paragraph describing a city street in the first minutes after heavy rain stops, focusing on sound and reflection.
Write a brief farewell letter from a lighthouse keeper to the lighthouse itself, on the day automation makes the job obsolete.
Describe the experience of learning to ride a bicycle from the point of view of the bicycle, in one paragraph.
Write the opening paragraph of a mystery novel set in a botanical garden during a winter storm, ending on a question.
Explain to a curious ten-year-old why the sky changes color at sunset, using one everyday comparison and no equations.
Write a product description for an alarm clock designed for people who hate mornings, honest about the product's limits but still persuasive.
Compose a short toast for the wedding of two meteorologists, working in at least two weather metaphors without becoming ridiculous.
Write a paragraph arguing that handwritten letters still matter in the age of instant messaging, aimed at a skeptical teenager.
Describe an abandoned railway station a century after the last train departed, in one paragraph rich with sensory detail.
Write a short dialogue between a barista and a customer who is clearly having the best day of their life, without either character saying why.
Invent a folk explanation for why cats purr, written as a two-paragraph legend passed down in a fishing village.
Write the acceptance speech of someone winning an award for the world's most boring hobby, played completely straight.
Describe the moment an orchestra tunes before a concert, from the perspective of someone attending live music for the first time.
Write a persuasive paragraph convincing your neighborhood to plant fruit trees along the street, anticipating one practical objection and answering it.
Write a diary entry from an astronaut's first full day on a Mars base, focused on one small unexpected domestic problem.
Compose a paragraph in praise of taking the slow train, written to persuade a friend who always flies.
Write a two-paragraph story in which the first paragraph is told by an optimist and the second retells the same events as a pessimist.
Describe a grandmother's kitchen using only concrete nouns and sensory details, naming no emotions directly, in one paragraph.
Write a review of a restaurant that serves only breakfast food at dinner time, from a critic who walked in skeptical.
Write a short monologue for a museum night guard who has grown fond of one particular painting, revealing which painting only in the final line.
